body.statement:
Assume \(L_r>0\), and define
\[
 d_{\max}=\begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M,
 \end{cases}
\]
\[
 x(d)=\begin{cases}
 \sqrt{d/L_r},&d\le M^2/L_r,\\
 \{d+M^2/L_r\}/(2M),&d>M^2/L_r,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad a(d)=1-x(d),
\]
and
\[
 H(a)=\int_a^1\frac{\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}}u\,du.
\]
For any \(0<d<d_{\max}\), select the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair with start \(a(d)\), and put
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}.
\]
If \(\limsup_n\gamma_n\le\alpha\), then, under each sign,
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
\]
This bound is attained asymptotically by the exact randomized allocation inside the selected two-sign pair.  Jointly over deterministic intensity profiles in \(\mathcal Q\) and late-void two-sign residual witnesses that vanish on \([0,a]\), are bounded by \(M\), and have Lipschitz modulus at most \(L_r\), the displayed expression is the optimized late-void envelope at diameter \(d\).

The residual elbow is \(d_r=M^2/L_r\) and is interior exactly when \(L_r>M\).  When \(L_q>c/2\), put \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\); the additional intensity elbow is
\[
 d_q=d(1-u_q)=d\!\left(1-\frac{c}{2L_q}\right).
\]
When both elbows are interior, either ordering \(d_q<d_r\) or \(d_r<d_q\) is possible.  The function \(H\) has the explicit forms
\[
 H(a)=c\log(1/a)-L_q(1-a),\qquad 0\le L_q\le c/2,
\]
and, for \(L_q>c/2\),
\[
 H(a)=
 \begin{cases}
 (c/2)\log(1/a),&a\ge u_q,\\
 c\log(u_q/a)-L_q(u_q-a)+(c/2)\log(1/u_q),&a<u_q.
 \end{cases}
\]
No full-structured-class honesty premise or global minimax attainment is claimed for this joint-intensity result.
body.proof_tex:
The right-Riemann calculation in the sharp joint-pair theorem gives the continuous strictly increasing separation map
\[
 d(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L_rx^2,&L_rx\le M,\\
 2Mx-M^2/L_r,&L_rx>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
Its endpoint value is \(d_{\max}\).  Solving \(d=d(x)\) on each branch proves the displayed inverse \(x(d)\), and for \(0<d<d_{\max}\),
\[
 x(d)\in(0,1),\qquad a(d)=1-x(d)\in(0,1),
 \qquad d(x(d))=d.
\]

Fix this selected pair.  The finite common-subprobability inequality gives
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+,
\]
while the same theorem gives
\[
 \Delta_n^\star\ge d(x(d))=d,
 \qquad
 \eta_n^\star\longrightarrow\exp\{-H(a(d))\}.
\]
Thus
\[
 \{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 \subseteq\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}.
\]
Using \(\limsup_n\gamma_n\le\alpha\) and continuity of the positive-part map yields
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[\exp\{-H(a(d))\}-2\alpha]_+,
\]
which is the stated formula because \(a(d)=1-x(d)\).  The randomized allocation from the sharp theorem has miscoverage at most \(\alpha\) and selects its only positive-diameter output with probability \([\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+\).  Since that output has diameter \(\Delta_n^\star\ge d\), its probability converges to the lower envelope.  This proves attainment within the selected pair only.

We now certify joint optimality of the witness.  If an admissible late-void residual pair starts at \(a'=1-x'\) and has limiting causal separation at least \(d\), boundedness and Lipschitz continuity imply pointwise
\[
 |g(u)|\le\min\{L_r(u-a')_+,M\}.
\]
Consequently its limiting separation is at most \(d(x')\).  Since \(d\) is strictly increasing,
\[
 d\le d(x')\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x'\ge x(d)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a'\le a(d).
\]
For fixed \(a'\), pointwise minimality of \(\bar q_\star\) in \(\mathcal Q\) shows that no other deterministic admissible intensity has a larger late-void probability.  Moreover, because \(\bar q_\star(u)>0\),
\[
 H(a_1)-H(a_2)=\int_{a_1}^{a_2}\frac{\bar q_\star(u)}u\,du>0
 \quad\text{whenever }0<a_1<a_2<1.
\]
Thus \(\omega(a)=e^{-H(a)}\) is strictly increasing in \(a\), and
\[
 \omega(a')\le\omega(a(d)).
\]
The clipped residual at \(a(d)\) and \(\bar q_\star\) attain both inequalities, establishing the joint late-void certificate.

The residual formula changes branch when \(x=M/L_r\), whose image is \(d_r=M^2/L_r\); this point lies in \((0,1)\) exactly when \(L_r>M\).  If \(L_q>c/2\), the intensity changes branch at \(a=u_q=c/(2L_q)\).  Since \(a=1-x\), its image on the diameter scale is \(d_q=d(1-u_q)\).  There is no forced ordering.  For example, with \(c=M=1\), \(L_r=2\), and \(L_q=3/5\),
\[
 1-u_q=\frac16<\frac{M}{L_r}=\frac12,
\]
so \(d_q<d_r\).  With \(c=M=1\), \(L_r=4\), and \(L_q=1\),
\[
 \frac{M}{L_r}=\frac14<1-u_q=\frac12,
\]
so \(d_r<d_q\).  The explicit formulas for \(H\) were derived by direct integration in the sharp joint-pair theorem.  None of these arguments uses all-horizon membership in the structured profile-contract class.
body.justification: This is the joint intensity-and-residual late-void frontier under honesty on the selected two-law experiment, the strongest conclusion that does not assume an unavailable all-horizon profile contract.
body.gap: The constant-intensity frontier does not optimize common void mass over the anchored Lipschitz intensity class; the pointwise-minimal profile introduces a second, intensity-driven elbow.
body.consumer: For a selected rare-arm pair, trial designers can read off the strongest late-void diameter obstruction allowed jointly by the intensity and residual profile constraints, without treating it as a full-class positive theorem.
